# Bondi

> Bondi is a native macOS system monitor with on-device AI. It tells you why your Mac is slow, in one plain sentence. It's made by Jabble Super Intelligence Inc.

- Status: the beta is launching soon, and the full launch follows it. Bondi can't be bought yet.
- What it does: groups every running process under the app that started it, finds what's holding memory, warns about one cause at a time and asks before it quits or stops anything, and keeps 30 days of history on the Mac.
- AI: runs on the Mac. On Macs with Apple Intelligence (macOS 26, Apple silicon) it uses Apple's on-device foundation model. Other Macs can download a small open model (Qwen2.5 0.5B) from Settings. Bondi computes every number itself, and the AI only writes the words around them.
- Data: history stays in a file on the Mac. The app contacts Jabble's server only to check its trial or license and to look for updates. There's no account and no analytics.
- Category: a system monitor and task manager for Mac, and an Activity Monitor alternative.
- Requirements: macOS 15 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel: MacBook Air, MacBook Pro, iMac, Mac mini, Mac Studio and Mac Pro.
- Pricing at full launch: a 7-day free trial, then a one-time purchase for one Mac, with no subscription. The first 250 licenses cost $6.99, and after that the price is $29.99. Paddle is the merchant of record. Refunds are available within 14 days.

## How Bondi compares
| | Bondi | Activity Monitor | iStat Menus | Stats | Vitals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tells you why your Mac is slow, in a plain sentence | Yes (on-device AI) | — | — | — | — |
| Explains what each macOS process is | Yes (125 processes) | — | — | — | — |
| Dev servers, grouped by project | Yes | — | — | — | Yes |
| Local AI models (LM Studio, Ollama) | Yes | — | — | — | — |
| Fan control | Yes (Fan boost) | — | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Lives in the menu bar | Yes | — | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Price | $29.99 once ($6.99 for the first 250) | Free, built into macOS | $11.99 once | Free, open source | $29 once |

Checked against each app's own website (apple.com, bjango.com, github.com/exelban/stats and vitalsmac.com) on October 4, 2026. "—" means it wasn't found there.

## Guides: Why is my Mac slow?
- [Why is my Mac so slow? How to find the real cause](https://trybondi.app/blog/why-is-my-mac-slow.md): Mac running slow? It usually comes down to one of a handful of causes. Here's how to tell which one it is, with real readings from a real MacBook Pro.
- [Why is my Mac slow after a macOS update?](https://trybondi.app/blog/mac-slow-after-update.md): Mac slow after a macOS Sequoia or Tahoe update? It's re-indexing Spotlight, re-scanning photos and syncing iCloud. Here's what's running and how long it lasts.
- [Is Spotlight indexing slowing down your Mac?](https://trybondi.app/blog/spotlight-indexing-slow-mac.md): When mds_stores and mdworker are busy, Spotlight is rebuilding its index. Here's how to tell, how long it lasts, and how to keep folders out of it.

## Guides: Memory
- [What is using memory on my Mac?](https://trybondi.app/blog/which-app-is-using-my-mac-memory.md): Apps like Chrome split into dozens of helper processes, so Activity Monitor hides the real total. Here's how to see which app is really using your Mac's memory.
- [Memory pressure on Mac: what yellow and red mean](https://trybondi.app/blog/memory-pressure-explained.md): "Memory Used" being high is normal on a Mac. Memory pressure, swap and compressed memory tell you whether you actually need more. Here's how to read them.
- [What is unified memory on a Mac? Unified memory vs RAM](https://trybondi.app/blog/unified-memory-mac.md): Unified memory is the RAM in Apple silicon Macs, shared by the processor, graphics and Neural Engine. What it means, how it differs from RAM and storage, and how much you need.

## Guides: Heat, fans and busy processes
- [Why is my Mac so hot and loud?](https://trybondi.app/blog/mac-fans-loud.md): Loud fans on a MacBook or any Mac mean the chip is working hard or running hot. Here's how to find what's heating it, and what to do if they won't settle.
- [kernel_task high CPU on Mac? Your Mac is cooling itself down](https://trybondi.app/blog/kernel-task-high-cpu.md): kernel_task at high CPU usually means your Mac is hot, and macOS is slowing apps on purpose to cool it. Here's why it happens and what actually helps.
- [WindowServer using high CPU on Mac: what it means and what helps](https://trybondi.app/blog/windowserver-high-cpu.md): WindowServer draws everything on your Mac's screens. Here's why it gets busy, what normal looks like, and the settings that actually calm it down.

## Guides: Mac tools and shortcuts
- [Task manager for Mac: how to open it, and the shortcut](https://trybondi.app/blog/task-manager-for-mac.md): The Mac's task manager is Activity Monitor. Here's how to open it on a MacBook or any Mac, the shortcut that works like Ctrl-Alt-Delete, and how to end a stuck process.
- [How to force quit on a Mac, even when it's frozen](https://trybondi.app/blog/force-quit-mac.md): How to force quit an app on a MacBook or any Mac: the keyboard shortcut, three other ways, and what to do when the whole screen is frozen.
- [How to check uptime on a Mac](https://trybondi.app/blog/check-mac-uptime.md): Three ways to see how long your Mac or MacBook has been running since its last restart, what the uptime command's numbers mean, and whether a long uptime matters.

## Bondi's Mac guide: what is this process?
- [What is apsd on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/apsd.md): apsd is Apple's push notification service on your Mac. What it does, why it's rarely busy, and what to do when apsd asks for your keychain password.
- [What is backupd on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/backupd.md): backupd runs Time Machine backups on your Mac. Why it uses CPU during a backup, what backupd-helper is, and how to stop a backup safely.
- [What is cloudd on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/cloudd.md): cloudd syncs your data with iCloud for Apple's apps and iCloud Drive. Why cloudd uses high CPU on a Mac, and what to do when a sync seems stuck.
- [What is CommCenter on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/commcenter.md): CommCenter handles phone calls and text messages that work with your iPhone on a Mac. Why it asks for your keychain, and whether CommCenter is a virus.
- [What is coreaudiod on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/coreaudiod.md): coreaudiod handles all sound on your Mac. Why it uses CPU, how to restart coreaudiod when the sound stops or crackles, and why you shouldn't quit it.
- [What is fileproviderd on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/fileproviderd.md): fileproviderd connects iCloud Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox and other cloud storage to Finder. Why it uses high CPU or memory, especially while OneDrive syncs.
- [What is fseventsd on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/fseventsd.md): fseventsd keeps a record of file changes for Time Machine, Spotlight and other apps. Why fseventsd uses CPU or memory during builds, downloads and unpacking.
- [What is launchd on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/launchd.md): launchd is the first process macOS starts, and it starts every other service. Why launchd is rarely busy, and what high CPU from it usually means.
- [What is loginwindow on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/loginwindow.md): loginwindow is your Mac's login session. Why loginwindow can use hundreds of MB of memory, what loginwindow Secure Input means, and why not to quit it.
- [What is mDNSResponder on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/mdnsresponder.md): mDNSResponder finds devices on your network and looks up web addresses for every app. Why it uses network or CPU, how to restart it, and why not to disable it.
- [What is mds_stores on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/mds-stores.md): mds_stores is Spotlight's indexer. Why it uses high CPU, memory or disk on your Mac, how long indexing takes, and how to keep folders out of it.
- [What is mdworker (mdworker_shared) on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/mdworker.md): mdworker and mdworker_shared are Spotlight's helpers that read your files. Why there are many copies, why they use high CPU, and when they settle.
- [What is mediaanalysisd on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/mediaanalysisd.md): mediaanalysisd analyzes photos and videos on your Mac for search, Live Text and Visual Look Up. Why it uses CPU, memory and storage, and what to leave alone.
- [What is photoanalysisd on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/photoanalysisd.md): photoanalysisd analyzes your Photos library for people, places and Memories. Why it uses CPU after imports, and whether you can disable or stop it.
- [What is rapportd on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/rapportd.md): rapportd lets your Apple devices nearby find and talk to each other for Handoff and Continuity. Why it asks to accept incoming connections, and whether to allow it.
- [What is spindump on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/spindump.md): spindump records what an app was doing when it stopped responding. Why it uses CPU right after a hang, and where its reports go.
- [What is syspolicyd on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/syspolicyd.md): syspolicyd is Gatekeeper: it checks apps the first time you open them. Why syspolicyd uses CPU on your Mac, and why it's busy for developers.
- [What is SystemUIServer on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/systemuiserver.md): SystemUIServer runs some of the menu bar's icons on your Mac. Why it's rarely busy, and how to restart it when menu bar icons stop responding.
- [What is trustd on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/trustd.md): trustd checks the security certificates of the websites and servers your apps connect to. Why trustd uses CPU on a Mac, and why several copies are normal.
- [What is XProtect (XprotectService) on Mac?](https://trybondi.app/guide/xprotectservice.md): XProtect is Apple's built-in malware protection on every Mac. What XprotectService does, why it uses CPU, and why you should leave it running.
